strong.name: Strong
strong.definition: Meta-analyses of classroom studies show that working this way improves learning.

promising.name: Promising
promising.definition: Controlled studies show gains, but results are mixed, small in number or dependent on context.

framework.name: Framework
framework.definition: A useful structure. The method itself has not been tested in intervention studies.

choosewise.name: Choosewise
choosewise.definition: Our own rule, not a research finding.

hero.title: What a plan looks like
hero.note: Our example, not a tested plan.

rows.text: In science, loses track of practical tasks with several steps.
The steps numbered on the board, a checklist on each table, the first step shown.
A quick check after step two with the students who still lose track.
Do they finish the practical without asking what comes next?

how: Name what you see in the task, in plain words: what happens, not who it happens to.
Find the closest barrier and use the whole-class moves first. They lower the barrier for everyone, and most students need nothing more.
Add one targeted support for the students who still meet it, decide what you will take away first, and set a date to look again.

barriers_intro.diagnosis: Have a diagnosis in mind? Two students with the same diagnosis can need very different things, and many students who need support have none. Describe what you see in this task instead, and pick the closest barrier below.
barriers_intro.privacy: Describe the task and the barrier, never the student.

cards.barrier: Doesn't get started on the task
signs: Waits after the task is set
Asks what to do when the others have started
Starts late, or only once you come over
cards.label: framework

whole_class.text: Show the first step and do it together, so everyone has started before anyone works alone.
whole_class.short: show the first step and do it together before anyone works alone

whole_class.text: Put a worked example on the board. Worked examples help learners with little prior knowledge most (0.51, a moderate effect).
whole_class.short: a worked example on the board
whole_class.label: strong

whole_class.text: Write the steps as a short checklist that students tick off.
whole_class.short: the steps as a short checklist that students tick off
whole_class.label: framework

targeted.text: A check after the first few minutes with the students who have not started: give them the first step, then move on (our suggestion, not a research finding).
targeted.short: a check after the first few minutes with the students who have not started, giving them the first step

not_this: Less work as the default. There is little evidence for it, and it risks lowering expectations.
cards.review: Do they start within the first few minutes without asking what to do?

sources.text: Tetzlaff, Simonsmeier, Peters & Brod 2025, Learning and Instruction
EEF 2020, Special Educational Needs in Mainstream Schools
Harrison et al. 2013, Review of Educational Research

cards.barrier: Loses track of instructions with several steps
signs: Does the first step, then stops
Asks what comes next
Skips steps or does them in the wrong order
cards.label: framework

whole_class.text: Number the steps on the board and leave them up for the whole task.
whole_class.short: the steps numbered on the board for the whole task

whole_class.text: Put a checklist of the steps on each table.
whole_class.short: a checklist of the steps on each table
whole_class.label: framework

whole_class.text: Show the first step before students start. Splitting instruction into segments gives small-to-medium gains in multimedia learning.
whole_class.short: show the first step before students start
whole_class.label: framework

targeted.text: A quick check after step two with the students who still lose track (our suggestion, not a research finding).
targeted.short: a quick check after step two with the students who still lose track

cards.review: Do they finish the task without asking what comes next?

sources.text: Rey et al. 2019, Educational Psychology Review
EEF 2020, Special Educational Needs in Mainstream Schools

link.text: Pedagogy Compass: My lessons overload them

cards.barrier: Reading a long text takes all their energy
signs: Reads slowly and runs out of time
Can talk about the topic but not about the text
Gets lost in long paragraphs
cards.label: framework

whole_class.text: Teach the key words before the text, and give a glossary. Glossaries were studied with second-language readers.
whole_class.short: teach the key words before the text and give a glossary
whole_class.label: promising

whole_class.text: Add one picture or diagram that shows the main idea. Graphics raised reading comprehension by 0.39, a moderate effect, at all grade levels.
whole_class.short: one picture or diagram that shows the main idea
whole_class.label: strong

whole_class.text: Split the text into sections with one guiding question each.
whole_class.short: the text in sections with one guiding question each
whole_class.label: framework

targeted.text: Text-to-speech or read-aloud for the long text: 0.35 on reading comprehension for students with reading difficulties, between a small and a moderate effect. It gives access to the content but does not teach reading.
targeted.short: text-to-speech or read-aloud for the long text
targeted.label: promising

not_this: Colored overlays and dyslexia fonts. Better-designed studies of overlays show little benefit, and two studies of dyslexia fonts with children found no gain.
cards.review: Do they answer the section questions without help with the words?

sources.text: Guo, Zhang, Wright & McTigue 2020, AERA Open
Wood, Moxley, Tighe & Wagner 2018, Journal of Learning Disabilities
Abraham 2008, Computer Assisted Language Learning
Griffiths, Taylor, Henderson & Barrett 2016, Ophthalmic and Physiological Optics
Kuster, van Weerdenburg, Gompel & Bosman 2018, Annals of Dyslexia

cards.barrier: Starts written tasks but doesn't finish them
signs: Writes a good opening, then stops
Runs out of ideas halfway
Hands in much less than the task asks for
cards.label: framework

whole_class.text: Share the criteria before anyone writes, and show a model text once students have a first draft.
whole_class.short: the criteria before anyone writes, and a model text once students have a first draft

whole_class.text: Add a short planning step before the writing starts: the main point and what supports it (our suggestion, not a research finding).
whole_class.short: a short planning step before the writing starts: the main point and what supports it

whole_class.text: Offer sentence starters, and take them away as students manage. Frames should be faded, because scaffolding can quietly strip the demand out of a task.
whole_class.short: sentence starters, taken away as students manage

targeted.text: Let them say the answer to a partner first, then write it (our suggestion, not a research finding).
targeted.short: say the answer to a partner first, then write it

not_this: Less work as the default. Cut only volume that does not serve the goal.
cards.review: Do they finish the written task without you sitting beside them?

sources.text: To, Panadero & Carless 2022, Assessment & Evaluation in Higher Education
EEF 2020, Special Educational Needs in Mainstream Schools

link.text: Quality Ladder: model texts and criteria

cards.barrier: Loses focus during independent work or in noise
signs: Looks around or chats once independent work starts
Is pulled off task by noise or movement
Works well with you, drifts when you move on
cards.label: framework

whole_class.text: Seat students in rows for individual work. Rows raised on-task behavior during individual work, most for disruptive students, across 8 studies; let the task decide the layout.
whole_class.short: rows for individual work
whole_class.label: promising

whole_class.text: Teach the routines for independent work explicitly, and practice them.
whole_class.short: the routines for independent work taught explicitly

whole_class.text: Give a short reminder just before a known trouble spot (precorrection).
whole_class.short: a short reminder just before a known trouble spot
whole_class.label: promising

targeted.text: Specific praise when they get it right: say what they did.
targeted.short: specific praise when they get it right
targeted.label: promising

targeted.text: A quieter seat for independent work (our suggestion; we have found no study of "preferential seating" for ADHD).
targeted.short: a quieter seat for independent work

not_this: Fidget spinners. Attention in class got worse in a study of 60 young children with ADHD.
Accommodations written in by habit. A systematic review found very little evidence for the ones commonly recommended for students with behavioral challenges.
cards.review: Do they keep working through independent work without reminders?

Royer, Lane, Dunlap & Ennis 2018, Remedial and Special Education
Graziano, Garcia & Landis 2020, Journal of Attention Disorders
Harrison et al. 2013, Review of Educational Research

cards.barrier: Finds changes and unstructured time hard
signs: Gets upset or stuck when the plan changes
Struggles at the start of lessons and between activities
Drifts in group work without clear roles
cards.label: framework

whole_class.text: Put the lesson's plan on the board as a visual schedule, and point to it as you go.
whole_class.short: the lesson's plan on the board as a visual schedule
whole_class.label: framework

whole_class.text: Just before each change, say what is ending, what comes next and what to do (precorrection).
whole_class.short: a warning before each change: what is ending and what comes next
whole_class.label: promising

whole_class.text: Teach transitions as routines, and practice them.
whole_class.short: transitions taught as routines

targeted.text: A personal visual schedule. The studies are mostly single-case studies with autistic learners, so plan from what you see, not from a diagnosis.
targeted.label: promising

cards.review: Do they move to the next activity without stopping to ask what is happening?

sources.text: Knight, Sartini & Spriggs 2015, Journal of Autism and Developmental Disorders
Ennis, Royer, Lane & Griffith 2017, Education and Treatment of Children

cards.barrier: Can do it with you, but not alone
signs: Gets it right when you work through it together
Stops when you move on
Asks you to check each step
cards.label: framework

whole_class.text: A worked example, then a half-finished one, then their own. The EEF describes scaffolding as "temporary support" that is removed as students manage.
whole_class.short: a worked example, then a half-finished one, then their own
whole_class.label: strong

whole_class.text: Questions students ask themselves to plan, check and evaluate their work. Metacognition and self-regulation add about 8 months of progress in the EEF Toolkit.
whole_class.short: questions students ask themselves to plan, check and evaluate their work
whole_class.label: strong

targeted.text: A partly completed example with the next step left blank.
targeted.short: a partly completed example with the next step left blank

cards.review: Do they finish a similar task on their own without asking you to check each step?

sources.text: Tetzlaff, Simonsmeier, Peters & Brod 2025, Learning and Instruction
EEF Teaching and Learning Toolkit: Metacognition and self-regulation
EEF 2020, Special Educational Needs in Mainstream Schools

link.text: Pedagogy Compass: They can do it with me, but not alone

cards.barrier: Is still learning the language of instruction
signs: Follows when you show, loses the thread when you only talk
Knows the idea but not the words for it
Writes much less than they can say
cards.label: framework

whole_class.text: Teach a set of academic words intensively across several days. The IES practice guide for elementary and middle school rates the evidence as strong.
whole_class.short: a set of academic words taught intensively across several days

whole_class.text: Let students talk, then write, in content lessons. The IES practice guide rates combining oral and written language as strong too.
whole_class.short: talk before writing, with oral and written language in content lessons

whole_class.text: Give sentence frames, and fade them as students manage.
whole_class.short: sentence frames, faded as students manage

targeted.text: An elaborated version of the text and a glossary of the key words. Glossaries had a medium effect on comprehension and a large one on vocabulary, in studies of on-screen glosses for second-language readers.
targeted.short: an elaborated version of the text and a glossary of the key words
targeted.label: promising

not_this: Stripping the language out of the text. Simplifying removes the language students need to learn; elaborate instead.
cards.review: Do they use the key words in their own sentences without the glossary?

sources.text: Baker et al. 2014, IES practice guide: Teaching academic content and literacy to English learners in elementary and middle school
Abraham 2008, Computer Assisted Language Learning
Oh 2001, TESOL Quarterly

adapt.intro: Keep the same text and the same task for everyone, and add support that can be removed: explanations in brackets, a glossary, one picture, and sections with one question each. Elaborate rather than simplify, so students still meet the real words. Then take the support away, piece by piece, as they manage without it.

example.text: "Photosynthesis converts light energy into chemical energy stored in glucose."
"Photosynthesis (the way plants make their own food) converts light energy (energy from sunlight) into chemical energy (energy stored in a substance) stored in glucose (a kind of sugar)."
glucose, a sugar that plants make and use for energy. "The leaf stores energy as glucose."
What does the plant take in, and what does it make?
A leaf with arrows for the sunlight, water and carbon dioxide going in, and the glucose and oxygen it makes.

adapt.check: Check every definition and bracketed explanation; this is where errors slip in.

record.intro: Keep each record as a short cycle of assess, plan, do and review, written as needs and measures: what the student meets in school and what will be done, never their difficulties or a diagnosis. Plan one to three measures, each with an owner, a start, a review date and what you will look for then. On the date, keep, change or stop each one.
record.warning: This form never goes through AI. Fill it in by hand or in your school's system for records.

review_questions: Which measures were carried out, by whom and how often?
What have we seen in the task since we last met?
Which measure seemed to help most, and how do we know?
What does the student say helps, and what gets in the way?
For each measure: keep, change or stop, and who does what before the next review?

What support do they need to reach the curriculum?
What are their strengths and interests?
record.country_line: Rules differ between countries. Check what applies where you work before you decide, record or share support for a student.

unsupported.intro: Six adjustments that are often recommended but have little or no support in research, each with what to do instead.

items.title: Colored overlays and tinted lenses
items.research: A systematic review found that the better-designed studies show less benefit, with effects small or similar to placebo.
items.instead: Teach the key words before the text, add a picture, and offer text-to-speech for a long text.

items.title: Dyslexia fonts
items.research: Two studies of children with dyslexia found no gain in reading; in the larger one, with 170 children, most preferred Arial.
items.instead: Keep your usual font, and put the effort into the key words, a glossary and sections with one question each.

items.title: Fidget spinners as an attention aid
items.research: Attention in class got worse in a study of 60 young children with ADHD.
items.instead: Rows for individual work, routines taught explicitly and a reminder before a known trouble spot.

items.title: Extra time as a classroom support
items.research: Extra time is a test accommodation. In tests it tended to help all students, somewhat more those with disabilities; it is not a support for learning in lessons.
items.instead: In lessons, change the route: steps on the board, a worked example and a check after the first step.

items.title: Less work as the default accommodation
items.research: There is little evidence for it, and it risks lowering expectations.
items.instead: Keep the task and the goal, and cut only volume that does not serve the goal.

items.title: Matching teaching to a diagnosis category
items.research: The EEF notes that "two children with the same diagnosis can have very different educational needs as individuals".
items.instead: Start from the barrier you see in the task, and pick the closest card above.

unsupported.movement_note: Movement breaks are not on this list: whether they help in class is an open question, resting on lab data about working memory.

evidence.lede: Planning from the barrier rather than the diagnosis rests on expert guidance. Most of the moves it leads to have good evidence of their own.

items.title: Needs, not diagnosis
items.label: framework
items.text: The EEF's guidance on special educational needs says that for most students with special educational needs a diagnosis is "less helpful for teaching and learning than determining the pupils' educational needs". Labels also change what adults expect: in US data on about 11,740 adolescents, teachers and parents expected less of students labeled with a learning disability than of students who achieved and behaved the same without the label (an association, not a measured cause). Primary teachers asked about "dyslexia" tied how effective they felt to the belief that the condition is fixed; the wording "reading difficulties" did not have that effect.

sources.text: EEF 2020, Special Educational Needs in Mainstream Schools
Shifrer 2013, Journal of Health and Social Behavior
Gibbs & Elliott 2015, European Journal of Special Needs Education

items.title: Good teaching for all
items.label: strong
items.text: The EEF recommends five strategies for every student: flexible grouping, cognitive and metacognitive strategies, explicit instruction, technology, and scaffolding. In its words, "to a great extent, good teaching for pupils with SEND is good teaching for all". Several of the parts have strong evidence of their own: metacognition and self-regulation add about 8 months of progress in the EEF Toolkit, and worked examples help learners with little prior knowledge most (0.51, a moderate effect).

sources.text: EEF 2020, Special Educational Needs in Mainstream Schools
EEF Teaching and Learning Toolkit: Metacognition and self-regulation
Tetzlaff, Simonsmeier, Peters & Brod 2025, Learning and Instruction

items.title: Text-to-speech and read-aloud
items.label: promising
items.text: Text-to-speech and related read-aloud tools raised reading comprehension for students with reading difficulties by 0.35, between a small and a moderate effect. They give access to the content; they do not teach reading.

sources.text: Wood, Moxley, Tighe & Wagner 2018, Journal of Learning Disabilities

items.title: Visual schedules
items.label: promising
items.text: Visual activity schedules meet the criteria for an evidence-based practice for autistic learners, especially combined with systematic teaching. Most of the 31 studies were single-case studies, from preschool to adult, so plan from what you see, not from a diagnosis.

sources.text: Knight, Sartini & Spriggs 2015, Journal of Autism and Developmental Disorders

items.title: Rows and reminders
items.label: promising
items.text: Rows raised on-task behavior during individual work, most for disruptive students, across 8 studies; let the task decide the layout. A reminder just before a known trouble spot (precorrection) is classed as an evidence-based practice in a review of single-case studies from preschool to Grade 12.

sources.text: Wannarka & Ruhl 2008, Support for Learning
Ennis, Royer, Lane & Griffith 2017, Education and Treatment of Children

items.title: Pictures and diagrams
items.label: strong
items.text: Adding graphics had a moderate effect on reading comprehension, 0.39 across 39 experiments, "regardless of grade level". Pictures, pictorial diagrams and flow diagrams did about equally well.

sources.text: Guo, Zhang, Wright & McTigue 2020, AERA Open

items.title: Elaborate rather than simplify, and add a glossary
items.label: promising
items.text: In studies of second-language readers, elaborated texts were understood about as well as simplified ones, or better, and they keep the language students need to learn. We have found no meta-analysis of the comparison. Glossaries had a medium effect on comprehension and a large one on vocabulary, in studies of on-screen glosses.

sources.text: Yano, Long & Ross 1994, Language Learning
Oh 2001, TESOL Quarterly
Abraham 2008, Computer Assisted Language Learning

items.title: The same task, with scaffolds you can take away
items.label: promising
items.text: In primary school, differentiation gave small to moderate gains when it was part of a broader program or used computers, while grouping students by ability on its own had a small negative effect on the lowest attainers. A separate easier worksheet risks lowering the demand for the students who need the content most, so keep the task and add support you can take away.

sources.text: Deunk et al. 2018, Educational Research Review

items.title: Assess, plan, do, review
items.label: framework
items.text: The cycle comes from the EEF's guidance. Its evidence review found no systematic review of it in England, and only some positive evidence from US response-to-intervention studies. The needs-and-measures form on this page is ours, built on that guidance.

sources.text: EEF 2020, Special Educational Needs in Mainstream Schools

care.risk: A student becomes identifiable from the details
care.what_we_do: Describe the task and the barrier for "some students". In a very small class, use the card and skip AI.

care.risk: The reply suggests something unsupported or lowers the goal
care.what_we_do: Check it against the card's "Not this" and the list of popular but unsupported adjustments, and keep the same goal for everyone before you use it.
Follow the TAKE IT AWAY part of the reply, and look again on the review date.
Read every definition and bracketed explanation before you print.

care.risk: The barrier is not the whole story
care.what_we_do: If nothing changes by the review date, talk with colleagues and your school's support staff. Plans for one student belong there, outside AI.
